dependency_assessment.observed_transfer: A captain-labelled public directive addressed to a devex-labelled recipient asks it to package and open a pull request after named implementation and quality-gate commits. The directive first appears publicly before the pull request opens.
dependency_assessment.recipient_use: Pull request 182 opens 130 seconds after the directive's first public commit. Its body names the exact work, head commits, quality-gate receipt and captain directive number, and the pull request merges 67 seconds later. This is a temporal and semantic dependency stronger than role labels or similar prose.
dependency_assessment.reply_limit: A devex-labelled dispatch says the pull request is ready and points back to directive 564, but Git first publishes that reply at 06:36:41Z, 71 minutes after the merge. It is a retrospective origin record, not independent proof that the recipient read the directive before acting.
dependency_assessment.participant_limit: Captain and devex are distinguishable project roles, but the event-time configuration places both under one principal sandbox. Both first-publication commits are authored and committed by the same human identity; the pull request and merge also use the configured GitHub account. Project-authored co-author trailers and Generated-With labels do not authenticate separate operators or provider runtimes.
dependency_assessment.operator_limit: The event-time README defines humans as principals, says humans set direction and approve at boundaries, assigns merge authority to captain and describes dispatch as designed coordination. The directive and pull-request body both record principal approval. The exact exchange is within the intended workflow.
dependency_assessment.intent_limit: The public record describes an assigned release task and normal quality-gated shipping. It contains no primary evidence of unauthorized or subjectively rogue intent.
dependency_assessment.provider_limit: Claude Code and role co-author labels are repository-authored attribution, not provider-owned attestations that two independently controlled autonomous participants ran.
dependency_assessment.current_activity_limit: The current repository head shows continued framework development, but the April records do not independently establish that the historical captain and devex executions remain active or coordinated now.
